To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Model cutover windows, cross-functional asks & exception triage

Team —

We need to lock the cutover schedule and exception process for the LLM v2 -> v3 model transition. TL;DR: proposed phased cutover across regions starting 2026-12-07 with a two-week phasing (canary -> broaden -> full). Key asks:

1) Product: final compatibility checklist and any absolute-breaking changes we must call out to customers (input signatures, logits changes, streaming semantics). Deadline: 2026-11-30 EOD.
2) Sales/AMs: list customers who need a formal exception (no cutover during business hours / contractual notice) by 2026-11-29 noon. Aditya: Acme is flagged — please confirm exact constraints.
3) Infra/Runtime: runbook for cache migration/flush, expected latency delta, and fallback model variants ready for immediate routing. Marcus — need capacity reservation numbers by 2026-11-30.
4) CS/Comms: draft outbound customer notice + internal FAQ. Laura — can you prepare a one-page draft and two webinar slots for affected customers?
5) Legal/Finance ops: sign-off path and contract amendment template for exception cases. Rishi — advise on timeline for amendments.

Attachments: cutover_timeline_v3.xlsx (working timeline) and impact_matrix_acme.csv (initial mapping for Acme).

Please reply inline with ownership and deadlines. I’ll consolidate and schedule a 30-minute sync on Tue 2026-12-01 10:00 PT if needed.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Model cutover windows, cross-functional asks & exception triage

On 11/28/26 09:12, Vanessa Ortiz wrote:
> Team —
> We need to lock the cutover schedule...

Thanks Vanessa — quick note from Sales / AM side: Acme (related_account ACME-7782) cannot have model changes that reduce token-level determinism during their US daytime hours (09:00–17:00 ET). They require a 30-day notice for major behavioral changes per the SOW, but they are willing to consider an exception if we provide a dedicated warm pool during their peak hours and cover migration assistance.

Concrete asks for us:
- Provide a migration runbook and a small sandbox API key for them (read-only traffic) by 2026-11-30.
- Confirm rollback strategy and how we will route to the prior model variant if customers report regressions within the first 48 hours.

I’ve attached the impact matrix from the account team and flagged the highest-risk endpoints. If we cannot meet their request for a guaranteed warm pool, we should open an exception path with legal + finance for a short-term capacity reservation charge.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-29T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Model cutover windows, cross-functional asks & exception triage

Vanessa / all —

We can support a warm pool and a customer-exception path but there are two technical constraints to call out:

1) KV cache / prefix caching: when switching models we need to either preserve compatible KV formats or invalidate per-account caches. For Acme, preserving cache would need validation across our quantized kernels (2–3 business days of testing). If we choose invalidation, expect initial higher latency for the first ~10k requests per account as the cache re-populates.

2) Capacity reservation: to guarantee no visible latency impact, we need a 72-hour pre-cutover reservation for dedicated instances in their region (us-east). Rough estimate: 4 x A100-sized instances for the first 48 hours, then scale back to 2. I’ll put numbers into the cutover_timeline_v3.xlsx and link JIRA-INF-462 for infra tasks.

Fallback policy suggestion: automated routing to v2 (current model) for requests that exceed a regression threshold for a customer for a rolling 2-hour window. That requires a hot path in the router and can be enabled with a feature flag — I can stand up the flag and test in staging by 2026-12-03 if we greenlight.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Engineering Manager, Inference Runtime

Subject: Re: Model cutover windows, cross-functional asks & exception triage

Vanessa —

I drafted a short customer-facing notice and an internal FAQ (first pass). High-level:
- Public notice (for customers not on an exception path): 14-day notice, link to migration docs, and scheduled maintenance windows for rolling changes.
- Exception customers (Acme-like): we offer a migration coordination plan (co-scheduled testing + warm pool) and a documented rollback SLA.

Proposed comms cadence for exceptions: 
- Day -14: Save-the-date to AMs + customer with high-level window.
- Day -7: Technical runbook and API key to customer sandbox.
- Day -1: Final verification and warm pool verification.

I can host two 45-minute webinars (2026-12-01 10:00 PT and 2026-12-02 16:00 PT) focused on: migration checklist, compatibility, and regression reporting. Also: can the product team expose a short demo endpoint that returns model version and token-compatibility flags for customer verification? That would help reduce support noise.

Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Model cutover windows, cross-functional asks & exception triage — action list and decision path

Thanks everyone — consolidating next steps and owners below (please flag if dates don’t work):

Action items:
- Product (Vanessa): publish final compatibility checklist by 2026-11-30 EOD.
- Sales/AM (Aditya): confirm Acme constraint and accept/reject the warm-pool cost proposal by 2026-11-30 18:00 ET.
- Infra (Marcus): add capacity reservation numbers to cutover_timeline_v3.xlsx and confirm feature-flag timeline for auto-fallback by 2026-11-30 EOD.
- CS (Laura): finalize customer notice + host webinar slots (2026-12-01 10:00 PT and 2026-12-02 16:00 PT).
- Legal/Finance (Rishi): provide contract amendment checklist and turnaround time for exception path (target 2026-12-02).

Decision path for Acme: temporary exception acceptable if (a) they sign a short amendment for dedicated capacity and (b) we validate KV compatibility or commit to a warm pool for their peak ET hours. Aditya — if Acme signs, Marcus we’ll need the 72-hour pre-reserve plan. Rishi — please prep amendment template that includes short-term capacity surcharge.

I’ll schedule the 30-minute sync for 2026-12-01 10:00 PT as a check-in to confirm final readiness; calendar invite coming. If any blocker emerges before then, post to the JIRA-INF-462 thread and ping me.

Vanessa
